methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches AI training program for workplace professionals - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents peer-to-peer AI upskilling infrastructure outside major metros, creating potential for deep capability development in a region historically excluded from tech concentration—a critical test of whether distributed fluency can emerge through educational institutions.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA signals Richmond's attempt to build a secondary AI hub, but concentration in university-industry partnerships may reinforce capability clustering in metros rather than distributing knowledge to surrounding regions like Southside.

signals.title: In the data center capital of the world, residents ask who the AI boom is helping - NBC News
signals.signal_reading: Residents questioning who benefits from the AI boom reveals that NoVA's data center concentration is producing infrastructure without broad capability development or economic distribution—shallow engagement concentrated geographically, the worst of both dimensions.

signals.title: Residents share data center concerns with state senators during listening tour stop in Danville
signals.signal_reading: Danville residents expressing concerns to state senators during a listening tour highlights that AI infrastructure decisions are happening to Southside, not with it—communities experience impacts without gaining deep technical capability or meaningful participation in the AI economy.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: Pressure on Richmond's young workforce suggests rapid AI platform adoption creating broad but shallow engagement—workers using AI tools without deep technical mastery, which could either democratize capability or create fragile dependence on commercial platforms.
